author: Lindsey Holt
subject: Cloud repatriation - Strata sizing
body:
Attendees: Matthew Johnson (Dir Infra), John Spencer (Storage Admin), Shannon Levy (Infra Mgr); Orvane: Lindsey Holt, Vikram Allen

Background: MTPW is pulling workloads back on-prem from their hosted provider (cost + data sovereignty for the SCADA historian and GIS). Everything lands on vSphere in the Newark DC.

Sizing
- Current on-prem: Strata 300 Unified Array G3, 60TB, file shares + GIS. ~30% used. Sits on the isolated OT management network, so no call-home.
- Repatriated data: ~22TB today (GIS imagery, historian, asset mgmt DB, CCTV retention for treatment plants).
- Proposed: keep the G3 as the primary array, add 2 expansion units, assume 2:1 data reduction on DB/VM, ~1:1 on imagery and video.
- John wants an NVMe tier for the historian SQL, capacity tier for imagery.
- Growth assumption we used: ~0.4 TB/month. Matthew thinks CCTV retention policy (90 days) could change - flagged as risk. With only 60TB this array has no slack if that happens.

Next steps
- Lindsey to send BOM + 5-yr ProCare options; customer wants FMV through Orvane Financial Services
- Vikram to draft datastore layout and replication plan

author: Vikram Allen
subject: New ops site - replication design
body:
Shannon Levy re the new Newark-area operations site (expansion announced last month). ~180 staff, small server room (2 racks, 8 kW each).
- Wants local copy of GIS + asset mgmt; considering a Strata 300 G4 at the new site with async replication from the primary Strata 300 G3 in the main DC. Link is 1 Gb MPLS, ~40% average utilization.
- RPO 4h acceptable for GIS, 15 min for asset mgmt DB.
- vSphere at both sites, separate vCenters.
- Asked about backup at the new site - will use Vault replication back to Newark instead of a local appliance.
Will send a design sketch. No budget until FY24 per Shannon.

author: James Lefebvre
subject: Intro - Dominic Holt (CIO)
body:
Attendees: Dominic Holt (CIO), Spencer Iyer (VP I&O), Matthew Johnson; Orvane: James Lefebvre, Scott Wilson, Vikram Allen, Whitney Chavez (TAM)

Dominic's priorities (first 90 days)
1. Data center refresh - wants a 5-yr view, not piecemeal
2. AI pilot with Krista Bailey's engineering group (leak detection on pipe sensor data, predictive maintenance)
3. Zero-trust follow-through

Storage
- Scott walked through the primary Strata 300 G3 trend from John's exports: ~63% used, ~1.3%/mo, runway to 90% roughly 20 months. Any CCTV policy change shortens that a lot. Asked Dominic to approve call-home so we stop flying blind - he'll take it to security.
- Dominic: at his previous utility he ran Lumora and liked the subscription model ("never buy a controller again"). He's not committed to Strata. Wants options.
- DP team scoping a second Vault for later this year (9F844GL is filling) - Dominic OK in principle.

Other
- Budget cycle: fiscal year starts July 1, capital requests due to the commission in March. Anything big has to be in the March package.

Actions
- Scott: 3-yr capacity model + expansion vs refresh options before March
- Vikram: AI pilot reference architecture (Atlas AI, 1-2 GPU nodes)
- James: get on Dominic's calendar quarterly

author: Vikram Allen
subject: Storage consolidation workshop
body:
Attendees: Matthew Johnson, John Spencer, Lauren Liu (Dir DC Ops), Shannon Levy; Orvane: Vikram Allen, Scott Wilson, Lisa Bryant, Owen Kruger

Goal: FY25 storage consolidation - get the primary data off the G3 and a 3-yr plan in front of Dominic.

Current state
- Primary Strata 300 G3: ~80% of 60TB per John's export, growing ~1.3-1.5%/mo. Still no call-home. File shares + GIS + historian. ProCare decision this year.
- Strata 300 G4 PG3JFY2 (new ops site): ~25%. Separate workload.
- Vault DP8900 9F844GL ~77% (1.5 TB/mo); DP5900 G4 20LWM1F ~16%, just in.
- vSphere 8, ~40 hosts. VMware renewal pricing up sharply - Matthew wants fewer hosts/sockets, which pushes more data onto shared storage, not less.

Options
A) Expansion shelves on a new G4 in the main DC + migrate G3 data, retire the G3. Buys ~18 months.
B) New Strata 500 tier consolidating all three arrays + NVMe-only performance tier. 5-yr.
C) Do nothing until FY27 - not viable; Lauren agrees.
- Lauren: power in Newark row C is 10 kW/rack, B fits in current footprint.
- Lumora has been in twice. Matthew says they're quoting a subscription with a data reduction guarantee.

Actions
- Scott: price A and B incl ProCare (no opp yet - create one)
- Owen: host consolidation sizing
- Lisa: firmware remediation plan for the Vaults

author: Scott Wilson
subject: Storage quote cut from commission package
body: Option B quote didn't make the commission package - Matthew said they want to "see Lumora's subscription numbers first." Never got an opp opened for it, so it won't show as a loss anywhere. Not a Lumora win yet, but they're the reason it stalled. Primary G3 is at ~82% and nobody on their side seems worried.

author: James Lefebvre
subject: FW: Lumora proposal
body:
James,

Sharing in the spirit of transparency. Lumora's proposal (summary below) is for 150TB effective with a 4:1 data reduction guarantee, subscription billed annually, controller upgrades included. Dominic likes not having a capital ask every three years.

Before our July meeting I need your team's answer to three things:
1. Why expand an array that's going to be ~85% full by fall instead of moving to something with an upgrade program?
2. What's your real data reduction on our data (not marketing)?
3. What does it cost us to stay on Strata for 5 years including ProCare?

Thanks,
Spencer Iyer
VP Infrastructure & Operations
Meadow Trail Public Works

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Lumora account team
Subject: MTPW - Lumora storage subscription proposal
> 150TB effective / 40TB raw NVMe, 4:1 guarantee, evergreen controllers, migration services included...
